citations.narrative:
The facility failed to have all birds listed on their animals on-hand inventory.
An accurate record of animals on hand is essential for proper identification and ability to track and identify animals being
used in regulated activities, as well as aid in the detection of movement of animals upon relocation to a new site.
Record of Animals on Hand (other than dogs and cats) (APHIS Form 7019) and Record of Acquisition, Disposition, or
Transport of Animals (other than dogs and cats) (APHIS Form 7020) are forms which may be used by dealers and
exhibitors to keep and maintain the information required by paragraph (b)(1) of this section concerning animals other than
dogs and cats except as provided in § 2.78.

The metal enclosure housing an umbrella cockatoo has multiple areas of rust and flaking paint. In several sections,
corrosion has progressed to the point that the metal’s structural integrity is significantly weakened.
Excessive rust can compromise the structural strength, create rough and jagged surfaces that could injure the birds, and
prevent proper cleaning and sanitization, increasing the risk of contamination and disease.
The surfaces of housing facilities must be constructed in a manner and made of materials that allow them to be readily
cleaned and/or sanitized, or removed and replaced when worn or soiled. Interior surfaces and surfaces that come in
contact with birds must be: Free of rust or damage that affects the structural integrity of the surface or prevents cleaning.

An enclosure housing two hybrid macaws contained a nest box that was chewed, creating sharp points of wood.
Broken or sharp wooden points in bird nest boxes pose a serious risk to the animals using them. Jagged edges can easily
injure birds as they enter or exit, leading to cuts, damaged feathers, or infections that may threaten their health and
mobility. These hazards are especially dangerous for young birds, which may not yet have the coordination to avoid sharp
surfaces. Smooth, intact interior surfaces help ensure the nest box remains a safe refuge—allowing birds to rest, nest,
and raise their young without risk of injury.
Primary enclosures must be designed and constructed of suitable materials so that they are structurally sound. The
primary enclosures must be kept in good repair. Primary enclosures must be constructed and maintained so that they:
Have no sharp points or edges that could injure the birds.
This is a1st Re-License Inspection for a Class “B” license. The inspection and exit briefing were conducted with the
applicant.
All items must be in compliance within 2 more inspection(s) or by October 18, 2026 or the applicant will forfeit the license
fee and must wait 6 months to reapply. Please contact your inspector to schedule your next Re-License Inspection.
Regulated activity can continue under your existing USDA license until it expires on August 31st, 2026.
